[0] While SpaceX wasn't recovering rockets, it was quietly signing deals with AI companies. In February, Starlink's parent company brought xAI (which includes Twitter, now renamed X) under its umbrella. In April, SpaceX signed a deal with Cursor, a competitor to Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex. As of August 14, the acquisition has been completed. And SpaceXAI (the company's new name), with Cursor's help, recently launched Grok Bot and the Grok 4.6 model.

[1] Updated August 14, 2026: SpaceXAI has completed its acquisition of Cursor.

[2] Updated June 16, 2026: SpaceX acquired Cursor one week after becoming a publicly listed company.

[3] The following is an updated version of the original report:

[4] SpaceX strikes $10 billion deal with Cursor ahead of $60 billion acquisition

[5] Cursor has long been popular among software engineers who use Macs and code with AI assistance. It was one of the earliest services to connect large language model AI into the application development workflow.

[6] In April, SpaceX and Cursor said the two companies were "working closely together to create the world's best AI for coding and knowledge work."

[7] The original collaboration included SpaceX paying Cursor $10 billion:

[8] Cursor disclosed further details of the collaboration arrangement in April, before the acquisition was completed:

[9] "Cursor is partnering with SpaceX to accelerate our model training work. We launched Composer less than six months ago as our first agentic coding model. Composer 1.5 then scaled reinforcement learning by more than 20x. Composer 2 added continuous pre-training to achieve frontier-level performance at a fraction of the cost of other models. Every compute increase has translated into significant gains in model capability. We've always wanted to push training further, but we've been constrained by compute bottlenecks. Through this partnership, our team will leverage xAI's Colossus infrastructure to dramatically advance the intelligence of our models.

[10] The collaboration between SpaceX and Cursor has further strengthened a product capable of competing with Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex agentic coding software.
